top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced achievement (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) with a two-name allocation that is clean and a citation that can be scoped to the neutral-atom lattice, distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It has also yielded facts about nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings), not just a smaller error bar. P002 is a close second: a larger conceptual step, but its three-name credit must be confined to the quantum spin Hall effect, leaving Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the 3D work outside and with the HgTe experiment testing a proposal other than Kane-Mele's graphene one. No award is ranked last since two defensible prizes exist.
recusal_note: Long-time collaboration with the Lund attosecond group of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-authorship with Lund, ETH and Schuch; none of these people is credited in P001 or P002, and I have no tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. Disclosure only, no recusal apparent.
